status.description: A resolution has been taken, and it is awaiting verification by reporter. From here issues are either reopened, or are closed.

comments.comment: Contrary to LU-19729, this specific issue "FAIL: release changed ctime from xx to yy" on sanity-hsm test_24a only occurred when testing on RHEL10, so it looks specific to this distro.

After analyze, I think I found the root reason for cmtime failures.
It is the stale ext4-nocatime.patch:

static inline struct timespec64 ext4_current_time(struct inode *inode)
+{
+	if (IS_NOCMTIME(inode))
+		return inode_get_ctime(inode);
+	return current_time(inode);
+}
+#define current_time(a) ext4_current_time(a)

The newer kernel EXT4 FS module does not use current_time to set amtime with the current time any more. Instead it is using inode_set_ctime_current(). This function will be used to update ctime or atime in ext4_xattr_set_handle().
We need to update the ldiskfs patch for ext4-nocatime.patch to support newer kernel S_NOCMTIME for XATTR SET.

The LU-19729 should also be related to this bug.
Wow, in this case ti would be related to LU-19732, for which Hongchao pushed patch "LU-19732 ldiskfs: keep RHEL10.x not to update cmtime" at https://review.whamcloud.com/63529.
Closing as a duplicate of LU-19732.
